title: Gen AI Workflow: How to Actually Maintain Creative Control - Garrett Fry
author: corysama

comments.author: shlaifu
comments.body: this looks about as labour-intensive as doing it from scratch....

replies.author: corysama
replies.body:
It certainly is intense! I'd like to know how much time it took to just to set up the workflow. But, now that it is set up...

If you were making a long movie with a consistent character, you'd be better off working with a fully-textured model. But, for "I just need a few short shots." This seems like a win over sculpting and painting everything in the scene by hand. The main pain is in the compositing stage.

If you did need a long-form result, you could use the generated meshes and projected textures as a starting point to brainstorm and bootstrap fully fleshed-out models that you use in a traditional animation and compositing scenario.
